Top candidates: **Leaf_Mold** (yellow spots upper surface), **Powdery_Mildew** (yellow lesions), **Cucumber_Mosaic_Virus** (mosaic yellowing), **Verticillium_Wilt** (V-shaped yellowing).

Now viewing one reference per top candidate:

**Analysis summary:**

- **Test image**: Single tomato leaf on gray surface. Shows pale greenish-yellow patches on the upper leaf surface, with diffuse/indistinct margins. No white powder, no discrete small spots, no V-shaped brown lesions, no distortion.

- **Leaf_Mold ref**: Similar pale yellowish patches on upper leaf surface — matches the diffuse chlorotic spots with no definite margins described in the KB ("brighter yellow with indistinct chlorosis on upper leaf surface").

- **Powdery_Mildew ref**: White powdery coating — not present in test image. Ruled out.

- **Cucumber_Mosaic_Virus ref**: Distorted, crinkled/shoestring leaves with mosaic — test leaf is flat with no distortion. Ruled out.

- **Verticillium_Wilt ref**: V-shaped brown necrotic lesions with yellow surround — test image lacks brown necrosis and V-shape. Ruled out.

The pale greenish-yellow patches with indistinct margins on the upper leaf surface align best with **Leaf_Mold**.
